name: Mix News Tools
author: INformigados

sections.description:
Mix News Tools brings editorial controls, SEO and optional site utilities into one WordPress plugin for news sites, magazines and blogs.

Manage global settings in Appearance > Mix News and override supported display options for an individual post or page. The plugin works independently of the Mix News theme; automatic layout controls integrate with the theme’s corresponding components.

Editorial controls for posts and pages

  • Post metadata: show or hide authors, publication and update dates, estimated reading time and approximate view counts.
  • Categories and tags: choose visibility and placement above the title or below the content.
  • Article components: control featured images and captions, author biographies, sharing links, related articles, comments and navigation.
  • Independent sidebars: assign different published synced patterns to the homepage, archives, posts and pages, with individual overrides.
  • Advertising spaces: select published synced patterns for supported banner positions, or leave them empty for an ad-free layout.
  • Floating links: configure back-to-top and WhatsApp/email contact links, including side and colors.

In the block editor, use the native document settings panels. In the Classic Editor, use the individual-display meta box. Inherit follows the global setting; Show/Hide overrides it for that document. Custom builder templates retain their own layout.

Menus, homepage and presentation

With compatible Mix News templates, choose separate saved Navigation menus above the logo, in the main header and in the footer. Navigation Link and Submenu blocks offer 16 local decorative icons. Header search can appear on either side of either menu.

Control story images, categories, tags, dates and excerpts, including excerpt length. Choose page numbers or a progressive Load more button; native next-page links remain available without JavaScript or after a loading error.

The default sidebar can show selected categories and popular articles ranked by approved comments or recorded views. Views require the optional counter. Custom sidebar patterns keep their own content.

Manual placement in other themes or builders:

  • [mix_news_share] – sharing links.
  • [mix_news_reading_time] – estimated reading time.
  • [mix_news_related] – related articles.
  • [mix_news_contact] – the optional contact form.

SEO, XML sitemap and draft copies

Built-in SEO provides document titles, descriptions, Open Graph, Twitter Card metadata and Article/WebPage JSON-LD. Each post or page has fields for an SEO title, description, canonical URL and noindex preference. Empty fields fall back to the WordPress title, excerpt or opening text. Social metadata reuses the featured image.

SEO is enabled by default. Drafts, previews and protected content do not output this metadata; password-protected documents request noindex. Automatic descriptions do not execute content filters or shortcodes. Search engines choose their own titles and snippets; rankings and rich results are not guaranteed.

The native WordPress XML sitemap respects site visibility and excludes protected documents, noindex content and custom-canonical URLs while built-in SEO is active. Its index supports pagination.

Recognized SEO providers – Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework and Slim SEO – retain control of SEO output and the sitemap. Yoast SEO was integration-tested for this release; the other providers are detected through their identifiers. Existing editor fields are retained, without automatically migrating another plugin’s data.

Duplicate as draft creates an unpublished copy after a confirmation form, document-specific nonce and permission checks. It preserves content, featured-image references, terms, layout settings and supported Elementor Free metadata. SEO title and canonical URL start empty; comments, statistics, publication dates and unknown metadata are not copied.

Optional site services

Page cache, image conversion, contact forms, analytics/consent and HTTPS enforcement are off by default. Enable only the modules you need. Operational settings require administrator-level manage_options; Tag Manager configurations also require unfiltered_html.

Public page cache

Cache public rendered HTML after WordPress boots using an existing persistent object cache, APCu, Redis or WordPress transients. Redis/APCu require the corresponding PHP extension and available server support; unavailable backends fall back to transients.

Private or password-protected content, signed-in visitors, previews, search, unknown parameters/session cookies, carts, checkout, account pages and detected dynamic forms are excluded. Content and settings changes invalidate the cache. The plugin does not install servers, replace cache drop-ins, globally flush another cache or create executable cache files.

WebP and AVIF uploads

Convert new static JPEG/PNG uploads locally when the WordPress image editor supports the selected encoder. Configure quality and maximum dimensions. WordPress serves the converted file and native responsive derivatives; the original remains available in the media editor.

Unsupported, animated, failed or larger conversions preserve the original upload. Existing images are not batch-converted. Deleting an attachment also removes its retained original. No remote image optimization service is used.

Simple contact form

Enable the module, configure a recipient and add [mix_news_contact] to a page. The form includes name, email and message fields, required permission, an expiring signed token, a honeypot, replay checks and temporary rate limits.

Messages use WordPress email (wp_mail). An empty recipient uses the administrator email. Hosting email or an SMTP integration must be configured; a success response confirms submission, not delivery. No attachments or message database are provided.

Analytics, verification and consent

Configure Google Analytics 4 by measurement ID or Google Tag Manager by container ID. Integrations load only after analytics acceptance, never for signed-in visitors. Without JavaScript or with Global Privacy Control, optional tracking stays off. There is no arbitrary JavaScript editor or custom-script field.

Customize the consent text, retention period and links to your privacy policy, cookie policy and terms. Accept and reject appear at the first level; a footer button reopens choices. Revocation disables Google consent, removes recognized Google cookies and reloads when an integration was already loaded. It cannot undo data previously sent.

Google Search Console and Bing verification tokens produce meta tags without loading tracking code. Enter the verification content token, not the complete HTML tag.

Verified HTTPS

HTTPS enforcement requires a valid installed certificate, a secure REST response recognized by WordPress and a verified HTTPS login URL. Failed checks keep the option off. It uses temporary 307 redirects for HTTP GET/HEAD and runtime URLs. It does not issue certificates, set HSTS, migrate database URLs or rewrite server files. Configure certificates and trusted proxies with your hosting provider.

External services

The plugin itself has no telemetry or required external account. When you enable a Google integration and a visitor accepts analytics, their browser connects to Google through www.googletagmanager.com.

  • Google Analytics 4: loads the Google tag for your measurement ID. Depending on your property settings, Google can receive page URLs, referrers, browser/device information, identifiers, usage events and network data such as an IP address. Google Signals and advertising personalization are disabled in this plugin’s configuration.
  • Google Tag Manager: loads your configured container. Data collection and further destinations depend on the tags you publish there. Configure the container for the analytics purpose presented to visitors. Google advertising consent flags remain denied.

Review the providers you configure and describe their purposes in your site’s privacy policy:

  • Google Privacy Policy
  • Google Terms of Service
  • Google consent documentation
  • Google publisher consent requirements

Consent scope: the banner controls integrations configured by this plugin. It cannot automatically block code inserted by other themes, plugins or advertising patterns. It is not an IAB TCF/Google-certified CMP; Google publisher products can require a certified CMP in applicable regions.

Sharing and contact links open the chosen service only when a visitor follows them. WhatsApp/email icons use WordPress’ local Social Icons glyphs; no remote icon library, WhatsApp SDK or automatic message is loaded. Advertising patterns can load services selected by the site owner. Native Custom HTML permissions apply; the plugin does not grant script privileges.

Privacy and stored data

  • Views: optional aggregate page-load counts per public post, disabled by default. The counter does not store IP addresses, user agents, visitor IDs, cookies or browser storage. Counts are approximate; repeated loads and bots can inflate them. Signed-in visits, previews and protected/unpublished posts are excluded. While this plugin’s consent banner is enabled, counting waits for acceptance.
  • Contact protection: a salted/HMAC IP hash is retained for a ten-minute rate-limit window; a used-token marker lasts one hour. The form does not save raw IP addresses or message records. Host logs and recipient mailboxes have their own retention policies.
  • Consent preferences: a first-party cookie stores the choice, configuration version and timestamp for the configured retention period of 1-365 days.
  • Settings and content: deactivation/uninstall preserves options and metadata so changing themes does not erase existing data. WordPress handles expired transient cleanup.

Suggested privacy text is available through WordPress’ privacy policy guide. There is no automatic plugin installation or activation redirect.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, open Plugins > Add New and search for Mix News Tools.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate. Alternatively, upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  3. Open Appearance > Mix News and review the global settings.
  4. Enable only the optional services you need, then adjust individual posts or pages where required.
  5. If using the contact form, add [mix_news_contact] to your content and verify your site’s email delivery.

No additional plugin is required or installed automatically. The source language is English; translations are delivered through WordPress.org language packs, respecting the site/user locale.
sections.faq:
Is the Mix News theme required?

No. SEO, sitemap controls, draft duplication, optional services and manual shortcodes work independently. Automatic placement, menus and presentation controls require compatible Mix News template components. The Mix News theme also works without this plugin.

Where are the settings, and can I change one post only?

Open Appearance > Mix News for global defaults. In the post/page editor, use the Mix News document panels or Classic Editor meta box. Choose Inherit, Show or Hide for supported controls.

Can I use another SEO plugin?

Yes. When a recognized provider is active, built-in SEO output and sitemap controls stand down to avoid duplicates. Disable overlapping features elsewhere as needed. Developer integrations can use the mix_news_tools_external_seo filter.

Does Redis or APCu work on every hosting plan?

No. The PHP extension and required hosting service must be available. Otherwise, storage falls back to WordPress transients. Redis defaults to localhost:6379; supported environment constants are MIX_NEWS_REDIS_HOST, MIX_NEWS_REDIS_PORT, MIX_NEWS_REDIS_PASSWORD and MIX_NEWS_REDIS_DATABASE. Never place credentials in public content.

How can I check or exclude the page cache?

Inspect the X-Mix-News-Cache: MISS/HIT response header. Use Purge page cache after changes, if necessary. The cache respects DONOTCACHEPAGE; developers can exclude additional contexts with mix_news_tools_cache_eligible. Keep cache lifetimes shorter than counting-nonce validity; refresh at least daily if the optional view counter is enabled.

Will existing images be converted automatically?

No. Conversion applies to new static JPEG/PNG uploads. WebP/AVIF support depends on the server encoder. Originals are retained, and unsuccessful or larger conversions keep the original upload.

Why did my contact form report success but no email arrived?

The response means WordPress accepted the mail submission. Delivery depends on the host, mail transport and recipient filtering. Check your hosting email setup or SMTP integration, spam folder and recipient address. The plugin does not store a backup copy of the message.

Does the cookie banner guarantee legal or advertising compliance?

No. It manages this plugin’s configured analytics integrations and visitor choices. It does not automatically block third-party code elsewhere and is not a certified advertising CMP. Your obligations depend on the services, jurisdiction and site configuration.

Are Elementor Free and other themes supported?

Manual shortcodes can be placed in other themes/builders, and supported Elementor Free document metadata is retained when duplicating a draft. Custom builder templates keep their own layout. This release was checked with free versions of Elementor, WooCommerce, Yoast SEO and Contact Form 7; individual site configurations still need testing.

Can the plugin guarantee a perfect PageSpeed score?

No. Performance depends on hosting, content, images, advertising and other plugins. Optional modules let you enable only the features you use. Test the actual public pages after configuring them.

What should I do before enabling HTTPS enforcement?

Install a valid certificate through your hosting provider and verify HTTPS access, including the login page. If recovery is needed, deactivate the plugin or define MIX_NEWS_DISABLE_HTTPS as true in wp-config.php. The plugin does not install certificates or rewrite that file.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial release with editorial display controls, related articles, sharing and optional aggregate views.
  • SEO fields and metadata, native XML sitemap integration and safe draft copies.
  • Opt-in public page cache, local WebP/AVIF upload conversion, contact form, analytics consent and verification, and verified HTTPS enforcement.
